page.layout: One page of text, single column; woodcut headpiece at top; large decorated initial S at left of the opening verse; page number top right; catchword "A" at lower centre-right. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: SOLUS ego non sum, dum solus obambu-
Es, Deus: & tecum, sim licet umbra,
Verba loquor, linguâ nil expromente: sed aures
Verba loquor, nullis hominum vulganda: satisque
est Dicta fuisse mihi, nota fuisse tibi.
Ne tamen haec studio iactata putentur inani,
(Ut mos illorum quos fera bilis agit)
Sunt breuibus quaedam chartis commissa: negauit
Omne ferent punctum; non si meruisse ferantur
Haec pede stans uno non lusi carmina, ceu quos
Sed fessum releuo corpus dum forsan eundo,
Hac totum soleo sic me oblectare palaestra:

page.notes: Woodcut headpiece and decorated initial are ornaments, not transcribed. Underlining and ink marks on the first verses are manuscript/stains and were not transcribed. Ornamental "E" at the title line is part of the title. Some words in the opening verse are partly obscured by the decorative initial; the reading "SOLUS" and "Verba" in the second couplet are as best read.
